The device is designed to automatically distribute degradable spheres from an unmanned aerial vehicle for plant protection applications. Its automated operation enables efficient aerial deployment while reducing the need for manual intervention.

The device comprises three principal sections: a ranking portion, an adjustment portion, and a distributing portion. The ranking portion includes a rotating shaft, blades, a bearing, a sphere cabinet, a coupling, and a motor assembly. During operation, the motor assembly drives the rotating shaft through the coupling, causing the blades to move the spheres within the cabinet and arrange them vertically in sequence for subsequent delivery.

The adjustment portion is configured to accommodate spheres of different sizes. It uses bevel gears to control the position of adjustment sheets, thereby changing the available passage space according to the diameter of the spheres. This arrangement improves the adaptability of the device and helps maintain orderly sphere movement.

The distributing portion includes circular wheels, spur gears, a guide rod, and a motor assembly. The motor assembly drives the circular wheels through the spur gears, while the guide rod directs the spheres toward the discharge point. By controlling the rotational movement of the circular wheels, the device releases individual spheres at precise intervals. As a result, the system provides accurate, consistent, and highly automated sphere distribution for aerial plant protection operations.

The present invention relates to an automatic UAV-mounted device for plant protection using degradable spheres. The device is installed on an unmanned aerial vehicle and includes a storage unit, a ranking mechanism, an adjustment mechanism, and a distributing mechanism. During operation, degradable spheres stored in the device are automatically guided into the ranking mechanism, where they are arranged in an orderly sequence to prevent stacking, jamming, or repeated delivery.

The adjustment mechanism enables the internal conveying and discharge space to be adapted to degradable spheres of different diameters. Accordingly, the same device can handle multiple sphere specifications without extensive component replacement or manual modification. After alignment and size adjustment, the spheres enter the distributing mechanism, which releases them individually or in predetermined quantities at set time or distance intervals. The release frequency can be coordinated with the UAV’s flight speed, route, and plant-protection requirements to achieve uniform and accurate distribution over a target area.

By integrating sphere storage, alignment, size adaptation, controlled conveying, and timed release, the device substantially reduces manual intervention and improves operational efficiency. It also helps avoid missed distribution, repeated distribution, and blockage during flight. The device therefore provides precise, highly automated deployment of degradable plant-protection spheres while offering broad adaptability, reliable performance, and versatility for different crops, terrains, sphere sizes, and application scenarios.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a patent abstract for an automatic biodegradable sphere dispensing device mounted on an unmanned aerial vehicle, describing its ranking, adjustment, and distribution mechanisms and listing the numbered components.

**Abstract**

An automatic dispensing device (10) mountable on an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) (12) is configured to transport and distribute biodegradable spheres (14) over a selected area. The device includes a storage hopper (16) supplying the spheres to a ranking mechanism (18), which sorts, queues, and singulates the spheres according to size, position, or a programmed release priority. An adjustment mechanism (20) regulates the feed opening, dispensing rate, release interval, and discharge orientation in response to flight speed, altitude, location, payload level, or mission instructions. A distribution mechanism (22), including a metering rotor (24), actuator (26), and discharge conduit (28), releases individual spheres or controlled groups while reducing jamming and unintended discharge. A controller (30) communicates with a UAV flight controller (32) and receives data from a position sensor (34), altitude sensor (36), and sphere-level or flow sensor (38) to coordinate dispensing with a predetermined distribution map. An optional spreader (40) varies the trajectory or lateral dispersion of the released spheres. A mounting frame (42), power interface (44), and access cover (46) permit removable installation, servicing, and loading. The system provides automated, geographically controlled, and adjustable aerial distribution of biodegradable spheres containing seeds, nutrients, microorganisms, treatment agents, or other payload materials.

**Numbered components**

counterfactuals.prompt: Generate patent-style text for a UAV mechanism comprising a sphere cabinet, rotating shaft and blades, adjustable bevel-gear-driven sheets, and motorized circular dispensing wheels connected by spur gears.
counterfactuals.output:
## Title

**UAV-Mounted Adjustable Dispensing Mechanism**

## Abstract

A dispensing mechanism for an unmanned aerial vehicle (UAV) includes a substantially spherical cabinet defining an internal chamber, a rotating shaft extending through at least a portion of the cabinet, and a plurality of blades coupled to the rotating shaft. A plurality of adjustable sheets are arranged relative to one or more discharge openings of the cabinet and are actuated through a bevel-gear transmission to vary an effective flow area of the discharge openings. At least two circular dispensing wheels are rotatably supported adjacent a lower portion of the cabinet. The dispensing wheels are driven by a motor through a spur-gear transmission and are configured to meter and discharge particulate, granular, powdered, or pelletized material from the internal chamber. Operation of the rotating shaft, adjustable sheets, and dispensing wheels may be coordinated by a UAV controller to regulate material agitation, flow rate, and distribution pattern during flight.

## Detailed Description

Referring generally to a UAV-mounted dispensing mechanism **100**, the mechanism includes a spherical or substantially spherical cabinet **110** supported by a mounting frame **102** configured for attachment to an unmanned aerial vehicle. The cabinet **110** defines an internal storage chamber **112** for receiving material to be dispensed, including, without limitation, seed, fertilizer, pesticide granules, feed, powder, or other flowable material.

A filling port **114** may be provided in an upper region of the cabinet **110**, and one or more discharge openings **116** may be provided in a lower region thereof. The cabinet may be formed as a unitary shell or as multiple shell portions removably joined to facilitate filling, cleaning, and maintenance.

A rotating shaft **120** extends into or through the internal chamber **112**. The shaft **120** is supported by one or more bearings **122** carried by the cabinet **110** or the mounting frame **102**. A plurality of blades **124** are coupled to the shaft and project radially or obliquely therefrom. Rotation of the shaft causes the blades to agitate the stored material, break up bridging or compaction, and direct the material toward the discharge openings **116**. The blades may be fixed, replaceable, foldable, or adjustable in pitch.

The shaft **120** may be driven by a shaft motor **126**, or mechanically coupled to another drive component of the dispensing mechanism. In certain embodiments, the shaft motor is a variable-speed electric motor controlled in response to UAV velocity, desired application rate, material characteristics, or feedback from a flow sensor.

A flow-regulating assembly **130** is positioned adjacent the discharge openings **116**. The flow-regulating assembly includes a plurality of movable sheets **132**, which may comprise plates, shutters, vanes, or overlapping diaphragm segments. Each sheet is movable between a relatively closed position and one or more open positions to alter the effective cross-sectional area through which material passes.

The movable sheets **132** are operatively connected to a bevel-gear drive **134**. The bevel-gear drive may include a first bevel gear **136** mounted on an actuator shaft **138** and a mating second bevel gear **140** connected to a sheet-adjustment member **142**. Rotation of the actuator shaft is thereby redirected to move the sheets inwardly, outwardly, rotationally, or linearly. A sheet actuator **144**, such as an electric servomotor or geared motor, may selectively rotate the actuator shaft to provide continuous or stepped adjustment of the discharge opening.

In one embodiment, the sheets **132** are circumferentially distributed around a central outlet and move synchronously to define an adjustable aperture. In another embodiment, respective sheets independently control separate discharge passages, thereby allowing asymmetric material distribution to compensate for wind, UAV bank angle, or a desired application boundary.

A dispensing-wheel assembly **150** is located below or adjacent the discharge openings **116**. The assembly includes first and second circular dispensing wheels **152, 154**, each rotatable about a corresponding wheel axis. Each dispensing wheel may include circumferential pockets, radial ribs, blades, teeth, grooves, or recesses **156** configured to receive discrete quantities of material and release the material as the wheel rotates.

A dispensing motor **160** drives the circular dispensing wheels through a spur-gear transmission **162**. The transmission may include a motor pinion **164**, a first wheel gear **166**, and a second wheel gear **168**. The first and second wheel gears may mesh directly so that the dispensing wheels counter-rotate, or may be connected through one or more intermediate spur gears to establish a selected direction and speed ratio. The spur gears may be enclosed within a gear housing **170** to inhibit contamination by the dispensed material.

The dispensing wheels **152, 154** may define a nip or metering region **172** beneath the cabinet outlet. Material passing through the flow-regulating assembly enters the metering region and is transported by the rotating wheels toward one or more discharge channels **174**. The channels may direct the material downwardly or laterally to obtain a selected distribution width.

An electronic controller **180** may be communicatively connected to the shaft motor **126**, sheet actuator **144**, and dispensing motor **160**. The controller may independently regulate agitation speed, aperture size, and dispensing-wheel speed. The controller may receive information from one or more sensors, including a material-level sensor, shaft torque sensor, wheel-speed sensor, flow sensor, UAV position sensor, altitude sensor, or airspeed sensor.

During operation, the blades **124** agitate and convey material toward the lower portion of the cabinet. The bevel-gear-driven sheets **132** establish a desired outlet area, while the motorized circular dispensing wheels meter and discharge the material. Coordinated adjustment of these components permits the dispensing rate to remain substantially uniform despite changes in UAV speed, flight path, or remaining material volume.

## Claims

1. **A dispensing mechanism for an unmanned aerial vehicle, comprising:**  
   a substantially spherical cabinet defining an internal chamber and at least one discharge opening;  
   a rotating shaft extending within the internal chamber;  
   a plurality of blades coupled to the rotating shaft and configured to move material toward the at least one discharge opening;  
   a plurality of adjustable sheets positioned to vary an effective flow area of the at least one discharge opening;  
   a bevel-gear transmission operatively coupled to the plurality of adjustable sheets;  
   a plurality of circular dispensing wheels positioned to receive material passing through the at least one discharge opening;  
   a motor; and  
   a spur-gear transmission coupling the motor to the plurality of circular dispensing wheels.

2. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, wherein the plurality of adjustable sheets are circumferentially arranged and synchronously movable to define an adjustable aperture.

3. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, wherein the bevel-gear transmission comprises a first bevel gear coupled to an actuator and a second bevel gear coupled to a sheet-adjustment member.

4. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, wherein the plurality of circular dispensing wheels includes first and second counter-rotating wheels defining a metering region therebetween.

5. The dispensing mechanism of claim 4, wherein each circular dispensing wheel includes a plurality of circumferentially spaced pockets configured to receive and discharge measured portions of material.

6. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, wherein the spur-gear transmission comprises a motor pinion meshing with a wheel gear fixed relative to at least one of the circular dispensing wheels.

7. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, further comprising a controller configured to independently control a rotational speed of the rotating shaft, a position of the adjustable sheets, and a rotational speed of the circular dispensing wheels.

8. The dispensing mechanism of claim 7, further comprising a flow sensor, wherein the controller adjusts at least one of the position of the adjustable sheets or the rotational speed of the circular dispensing wheels based on an output of the flow sensor.

9. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, wherein the blades are oriented obliquely relative to the rotating shaft to convey material axially toward the at least one discharge opening.

10. The dispensing mechanism of claim 1, further comprising a mounting frame configured to removably couple the substantially spherical cabinet to the unmanned aerial vehicle.

11. **A method of dispensing material from an unmanned aerial vehicle, comprising:**  
    storing flowable material within a substantially spherical cabinet;  
    rotating a shaft carrying a plurality of blades to agitate the flowable material;  
    actuating a bevel-gear transmission to adjust a plurality of sheets associated with a discharge opening;  
    delivering the flowable material through the adjusted discharge opening to a plurality of circular dispensing wheels; and  
    driving the circular dispensing wheels with a motor through a spur-gear transmission to meter and discharge the flowable material.

12. The method of claim 11, further comprising varying at least one of a shaft speed, a position of the plurality of sheets, or a dispensing-wheel speed according to a flight speed of the unmanned aerial vehicle.

counterfactuals.prompt: Describe an automatic plant-protection sphere distributing apparatus for a drone, explaining how it vertically ranks biodegradable spheres, adapts to varying sphere volumes, and releases them at controlled intervals.
counterfactuals.output:
An automatic plant-protection sphere distributing apparatus for a drone can be configured as a lightweight, gravity-fed module with three main sections:

1. **Vertical ranking mechanism**  
   Biodegradable spheres are loaded into an upper hopper whose sloped walls guide them toward one or more vertical ranking tubes. Gentle vibration, an agitator, or a slowly rotating guide disk prevents bridging and directs the spheres into a single-file column. Gravity keeps the spheres vertically ranked above a lower dispensing outlet.

2. **Adaptation to different sphere volumes**  
   The ranking tube and metering chamber may use flexible liners, spring-loaded guide plates, or interchangeable sleeves to accommodate spheres of different diameters. An adjustable metering pocket can also be formed by movable sidewalls or an elastic cup. A sensor—such as an optical, mechanical, or distance sensor—detects whether a sphere is correctly seated, allowing the controller to adjust the chamber opening or agitator operation without crushing the biodegradable shell.

3. **Controlled interval release**  
   At the bottom of the column, a motor-driven escapement meters one sphere at a time. For example, two vertically spaced gates operate alternately: the upper gate holds the remaining column while the lower gate releases the lowest sphere, after which the lower gate closes and the upper gate admits the next sphere. A servo, stepper motor, or rotary pocket wheel can provide the same function. The drone’s controller triggers the mechanism according to a preset time interval, flight distance, GPS position, or ground-speed-compensated spacing.

Sensors can confirm each discharge and detect jams or an empty hopper. The controller may briefly vibrate or reverse the metering motor if no release is detected. Thus, the apparatus maintains a vertically ordered supply, handles variations in sphere volume, and deposits individual plant-protection spheres at repeatable, controlled intervals during flight.
